office_does: The assessor values all property in Skamania County for taxation, calculates the levy limits and rates of its taxing districts and administers exemptions; four-year term.
race_blurb: Democrat Gabe Spencer, assessor for about two decades, faces Republican Cora Moser, a county employee with 20 years as a paralegal, on her first run; the primary was 2,157 to 2,130 for Moser. Moser runs on a state homestead exemption and opposes what she calls the incumbent's plan to sell the fairgrounds parking lot; Spencer runs on defensible valuations and a higher business personal property exemption.

candidates.summary: Carson resident raised in Mill A; 20 years as a paralegal and more than eight working for Skamania County. Republican, endorsed by the county Republican Party; led the primary by 27 votes.
highlights: Would advocate for a state homestead exemption through the assessors' exemption committee [S2][S5]
Promises plain-language valuations and an open-door office [S1][S5]
Opposes selling the county fair parking lot, which she attributes to the incumbent [S2]
Not a certified appraiser; says she would seek certification if elected [S2]
Endorsed by the Skamania County Republican Party [S4]

taxes.basis: Makes property tax relief for homeowners (a state homestead exemption) her main goal for the office and promises to make property taxes 'more affordable', while noting the assessor does not set tax policy.

experience.basis: First-time candidate who asks for change and 'a fresh perspective' against a two-decade incumbent.

candidates.summary: Skamania County Assessor for about 20 years (in the office since 2002), running for re-election as a Democrat; unopposed in 2022.
highlights: Backs raising the business personal property tax exemption from $15,000 to $50,000 or more [S2]
Uses sales, cost and income approaches, taking the lower middle of the data for commercial values [S2]
DOR's 2025 levy audit found two procedural requirements and one recommendation for his office [S3]
Lost the primary to Moser by 27 votes [S4]

taxes.basis: His stated tax agenda is a larger business personal property exemption, pursued through the assessors' association, to let small businesses keep more capital; no position on new revenue.

experience.basis: Assessor for about two decades, re-elected unopposed in 2022, running on continuity of the office and its staff.
